This article describes the changes in enshrined deities and divine titles – such as those of the {{ill|Gongen|en|Gongen|qid=Q3080343|lt=Gongen}}, {{ill|Gion shrines|ja|祇園社|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祇園神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}, and {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} shrines – resulting from the Meiji Restoration’s {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離令|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q1970535|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1970535}} (also known as the “Shinbutsu Hannzenrei”) and subsequent {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}.
Subsequently, some temples and shrines have maintained their deities as they were, while others have restored or enshrined the previous deities alongside new ones. In addition, certain temples and shrines present the evolution of deities over time.
This is only one example; since there may be alternative theories regarding deities at various shrines, please refer to the detailed articles for each shrine.
== Gongen Changes ==
{{See also|List of Gongen}}
* {{ill|Atago Gongen|en|Atago Gongen|qid=Q1101132|lt=Atago Gongen}} → {{ill|Atago Faith|ja|愛宕大神|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 愛宕信仰|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11493823}} (Atago Ōkami)
* {{ill|Akiba Gongen|ja|秋葉権現}}: Sanshakubō Daigongen → {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|en|Kagu-tsuchi|qid=Q1640658|lt=Fire Kagutsuchi}} (Kagutsuchi)
* {{ill|Iinawa Gongen|ja|飯縄権現}} (Iitsuna Myōjin): {{ill|Dakini|en|Dakini|qid=Q1127224|lt=Dakiniten}} (Dakiniten) → {{ill|Ukemochi|ja|保食命|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q2280323|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2280323}} (Ukemochi)
* {{ill|Izuyama Gongen|ja|伊豆山権現}} (Sōyu Gongen) → {{ill|Izusan Gongen|ja|伊豆山大神|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135491724}} (Red-White Two Dragons)
* {{ill|Echichi Daigongen|ja|越知大権現}} → {{ill|Izanagi|en|Izanagi|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi}}
* {{ill|Konpira Gongen|ja|金毘羅大権現|lt=Konpira Daigongen}} → {{ill|Ōmononushi|fr|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|mni|ꯑꯣꯃꯣꯅꯣꯅꯨꯁꯤ|ru|Омононуси|simple|Ōmononushi|zh|大物主|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}}
* {{ill|Zaō Gongen|ja|蔵王権現|lt=Zao Gongen}} → {{ill|Emperor Ankan|en|Emperor Ankan|qid=Q241765|lt=Ankan Tennō}} (Hirokuni Oshiken Kin-nichimei)
* {{ill|Hakusan Gongen|ja|白山権現}} → {{ill|Kikurihime|en|Kikurihime|qid=Q11619891|lt=Hakusan Hime}} (Shirayama-hime)
* {{ill|Tateyama Gongen|ja|立山権現}} → Tateyama Daigongen (Yūyama no kami, Tōbi Tennjin, Tsurugi-dake no kami)
* {{ill|Ishibuto Daigongen|ja|石鈇大権現|qid=Q140446076}} → {{ill|Ishizuchi Ōkami|ja|石鎚大神|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|qid=Q135491726}} (Ishidohibiko, i.e. Ishizuchi)
Note: Even after the official abolition of the “Gongen” title, this designation continues to be used to refer to temples and their enshrined deities.
== Changes at the Tennōsha ==
* {{ill|Gion shrines|ja|祇園社|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 祇園神社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}: ({{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}}) → {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}
== Others ==
* {{ill|Suitengū|en|Suitengū|qid=Q125319456|lt=Suitengū}}: ({{ill|Suiten|ja|水天}}) → {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} (Ame-no-Minakanushi), {{ill|Emperor Antoku|en|Emperor Antoku|qid=Q316651|lt=Emperor Antoku}}, {{ill|Taira no Tokuko|en|Taira no Tokuko|qid=Q3315855|lt=Heitokushi}}, {{ill|Taira no Tokiko|en|Taira no Tokiko|qid=Q3379244|lt=Heijikoshi}}
* {{ill|Kumano Taisha|en|Kumano Taisha|qid=Q11568887|lt=Kumano Taisha}}: ({{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}) → {{ill|Kushimikenu-no-mikoto|ja|櫛御気野命|qid=Q140446077}} (Kushimikenu-no-mikoto)
* {{ill|Izumo-taisha|en|Izumo-taisha|qid=Q696362|lt=Izumo Taisha}}: ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} → {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}) → {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}}
* {{ill|Kanda Shrine|en|Kanda Shrine|qid=Q717682|lt=Kanda Myōjin}}: Taira no Masakado was excluded from the enshrined deities as a rebel (although he was reinstated as a deity in 1984).
Among these changes, there are cases where deities that had been syncretized or equated – such as Gion with Susanoo and Hakusan Gongen with Hakusan Hime – are involved; however, {{Citation needed範囲|Other changes have been made based on interpretations of texts such as the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}, resulting in modifications to represent deities of the same or similar divine nature.|date=2014th year 6月}}. In addition, because Suiten shares the common attribute of being both {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|en|Ame-no-Minakanushi|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}} and a primordial deity, it was changed, and Suiten itself came to be equated with {{ill|Emperor Antoku|en|Emperor Antoku|qid=Q316651|lt=Emperor Antoku}} (the Water Emperor) with whom it is jointly enshrined. Meanwhile, Kushimikenu-no-mikoto continues to be used as an epithet for Susanoo (and in some cases is also used as an alternate name for {{ill|Iotake-no-mikoto|ja|五十猛命}}).
